children: French state-owned utility EDF is close to finalizing a major civil engineering contract worth around €14 billion ($15.38 billion) with construction giants Bouygues
for its EPR2 nuclear reactors, French daily Les Echos reported.
Reuters could not verify the report.

The unprecedented joint framework agreement, which also includes mid-sized builders NGE and Fayat, will cover the construction of foundations and concrete structures across multiple planned reactor sites over a 15-year period, the report said.
The shared framework is aimed at standardizing work and securing around €800 million in cost savings.
EDF said civil engineering work discussions are ongoing with a consortium of major industry players. The construction companies did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

According to the report, the deal is set to be submitted to EDF's board of directors for approval by the end of the month, ahead of a formal investment decision on France's initial program of six next-generation EPR2 reactors expected in December.
It would mark the largest contract signed with third parties under this reactor programme, with previous deals struck with subsidiaries of EDF.
The project's state aid funding package still requires approval by the European Commission before EDF can take a final investment decision on the six new reactors.
